label: L14
title: Robust optimization algorithms
brief: Lecture 14 shows how to solve a robust LP max cᵀx s.t. aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ, which has infinitely many constraints. The direct method computes the worst case max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx in closed form: for norm sets aᵢ = āᵢ + Δᵢᵀuᵢ, ‖uᵢ‖ ≤ ρ it equals āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖_*, using the dual norm (ellipsoid → SOCP; box and budget → LP). The duality method turns the inner max into a min for polyhedral sets, giving an LP counterpart with extra variables pᵢ. Cutting planes alternate between a master LP over finite restricted sets and per-row worst-case subproblems until no constraint is violated, illustrated on robust nurse scheduling. Exams ask you to derive a counterpart for a given set, name its class and size, pair norms with dual norms, compute a worst-case left-hand side, and reason about the cutting-plane loop and when each method is faster.
kp: Robust row aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ ⇔ max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ: finitely many but ill-structured constraints.
Direct method: closed-form inner max g(x), then impose g(x) ≤ bᵢ.
Norm set Uᵢ = {āᵢ + Δᵢᵀuᵢ : ‖uᵢ‖ ≤ ρ}; ℓ1 budget, ℓ2 ellipsoid, ℓ∞ box.
Worst case = āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖_*, with ‖s‖_* = max_{‖x‖≤1}|sᵀx|; a safety buffer.
Dual pairs: ℓ∞↔ℓ1, ℓ2↔ℓ2, ℓp↔ℓq with q = p/(p−1).
Ellipsoidal counterpart is an SOCP with the same size as the nominal LP; box and budget stay linear.
Duality method: max = min via strong duality; min ≤ bᵢ ⇔ ∃pᵢ, so pᵢ become variables.
Polyhedral counterpart: āᵢᵀx + pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ, pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≥ 0; LP with n + Σℓᵢ variables, m + nm constraints.
Cutting planes: master over Ûᵢ ⊆ Uᵢ, add âᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ if âᵢᵀx* > bᵢ + ε, stop when no cut; needs no strong duality.
Benchmark: cutting planes tend to win on polyhedral sets, reformulation on ellipsoidal sets.

topics.n: Robust LP and the inner problem
topics.x: The robust LP max cᵀx s.t. aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ has infinitely many constraints; equivalently max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ, finitely many but ill-structured. The direct method solves the inner maximization in closed form, g(x) = max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx, and replaces the constraint by g(x) ≤ bᵢ.

Norm sets capture small deviations around nominal values: Uᵢ = {āᵢ + Δᵢᵀuᵢ : ‖uᵢ‖ ≤ ρ}, with Δᵢ scaling relative uncertainty and ρ the extent. ℓ1 gives budget, ℓ2 ellipsoidal, ℓ∞ box uncertainty. Element-wise deviations (−Γ ≤ uᵢⱼ ≤ Γ) and CLT-style global perturbations (−Γ√n ≤ Σⱼuᵢⱼ ≤ Γ√n) motivate them.

For a norm set the worst case is āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖_*, a safety buffer that grows with uncertainty. Ellipsoidal (ℓ2, self-dual) gives a second-order cone problem of the same size as the nominal LP; box (ℓ∞) gives an ℓ1 buffer and budget (ℓ1) an ℓ∞ buffer, both linear. In general ℓp pairs with ℓq, q = p/(p−1).

If the inner max equals a min over pᵢ ∈ Vᵢ, then 'min ≤ bᵢ' holds iff some pᵢ satisfies it, so pᵢ become decision variables. For polyhedral sets Uᵢ = {āᵢ + uᵢ : Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ}, strong LP duality gives the robust counterpart āᵢᵀx + pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ, pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≥ 0: an LP with n + Σℓᵢ variables and m + nm constraints.

Keep finite restricted sets Ûᵢ ⊆ Uᵢ, starting from the nominal rows. Solve the master LP, then for each row find the worst case âᵢ = argmax_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx*; add âᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ if violated by more than ε and re-solve (dual simplex), stopping when no cut is added. Applied to nurse scheduling, the subproblem finds the demand scenario h that maximizes the nurse-to-patient-ratio insufficiency.

Cutting planes need only an oracle for the inner max (no strong duality); reformulation gives one tractable robust counterpart for a wide range of sets. Benchmarks (Bertsimas, Dunning, Lubin 2016) find both competitive: cutting planes tend to dominate with polyhedral uncertainty, reformulation with ellipsoidal uncertainty.

cards.f: Three forms of the robust LP
cards.b: Nominal: max cᵀx s.t. aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ, x ≥ 0. Robust: aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ (infinitely many constraints). Reformulated: max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ (m constraints, ill-structured).
cards.x: Uncertainty is row-wise: each constraint i has its own set Uᵢ, so the worst case is taken row by row.

cards.b: Solve the inner problem analytically, g(x) = max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx, and replace the robust constraint by g(x) ≤ bᵢ.
cards.x: Works for well-structured, norm-based sets where the inner max has a closed form.

cards.b: Uᵢ = {aᵢ = āᵢ + Δᵢᵀuᵢ : ‖uᵢ‖ ≤ ρ, uᵢ ∈ ℝ^{kᵢ}}, Δᵢ ∈ ℝ^{kᵢ×n}, ρ ≥ 0.
cards.x: uᵢ is a small-norm perturbation controlling the extent; Δᵢ scales relative uncertainty across components.

cards.b: ℓ1 ball: budget uncertainty. ℓ2 ball: ellipsoidal uncertainty. ℓ∞ ball: box uncertainty.
cards.x: For the same ρ, ℓ1 ball ⊆ ℓ2 ball ⊆ ℓ∞ ball, so box is the most conservative of the three.

cards.b: max_{‖uᵢ‖₂≤ρ} uᵢᵀ(Δᵢx) = ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂, attained at uᵢ* = ρ Δᵢx/‖Δᵢx‖₂.
cards.x: Feasible (‖uᵢ*‖₂ = ρ) and optimal by Cauchy–Schwarz: uᵢᵀ(Δᵢx) ≤ ‖uᵢ‖₂‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≤ ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂.

cards.b: max cᵀx s.t. āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≤ bᵢ ∀i, x ≥ 0.
cards.x: A second-order cone problem with the same size as the nominal (n variables, m constraints): nearly as tractable as the LP. ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ is the safety buffer.
Measures how much s can 'stretch' a unit vector. It turns any norm-set inner max into āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖_*.

cards.b: ‖uᵢ‖∞ ≤ ρ → āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖₁ ≤ bᵢ. ‖uᵢ‖₂ ≤ ρ → āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≤ bᵢ. ‖uᵢ‖₁ ≤ ρ → āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖∞ ≤ bᵢ.
cards.x: General rule: ℓp is dual to ℓq with q = p/(p−1). Trap: the buffer uses the dual norm, not the set's own norm.

cards.b: If max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx = min_{pᵢ∈Vᵢ} g(pᵢ), then min_{pᵢ∈Vᵢ} g(pᵢ) ≤ bᵢ ⇔ ∃pᵢ ∈ Vᵢ: g(pᵢ) ≤ bᵢ, so add pᵢ as decision variables.
cards.x: A 'max ≤ b' needs every point; a 'min ≤ b' needs only one witness. Strong duality makes the switch exact.

cards.b: Uᵢ = {aᵢ = āᵢ + uᵢ : Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ, uᵢ ∈ ℝⁿ}, Dᵢ ∈ ℝ^{ℓᵢ×n}, dᵢ ∈ ℝ^{ℓᵢ}.
cards.x: Example: the CLT set −Γ√n ≤ Σⱼ(aᵢⱼ − āᵢⱼ)/σᵢⱼ ≤ Γ√n is polyhedral.

cards.f: Polyhedral inner problem and its dual
cards.b: Primal: max uᵢᵀx s.t. Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ. Dual: min pᵢᵀdᵢ s.t. pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≥ 0. Robust constraint ⇔ ∃pᵢ ≥ 0: pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, āᵢᵀx + pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ.
cards.x: uᵢ free ⇒ dual equality constraints; Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ in a max ⇒ pᵢ ≥ 0.

cards.f: Size of the polyhedral robust counterpart
cards.b: An LP with n + Σᵢℓᵢ variables, m + nm regular constraints and n + Σᵢℓᵢ nonnegativity constraints (nominal: n variables, m constraints).
cards.x: Size grows with the uncertainty-set description, unlike the ellipsoidal counterpart, but is generally tractable in practice.

cards.b: Master: max cᵀx s.t. aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Ûᵢ, x ≥ 0, with Ûᵢ ⊆ Uᵢ finite. Subproblem (per row): âᵢ = argmax_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx*; Ûᵢ ← Ûᵢ ∪ {âᵢ}.
cards.x: The master is a relaxation of the robust problem; the subproblem either certifies x* robust feasible (hence optimal) or returns a cut.

cards.b: 1. Ûᵢ = {āᵢ} (nominal). 2. Solve master: infeasible ⇒ robust infeasible; unbounded ⇒ take x* with very large objective. 3. For each i, âᵢ = argmax aᵢᵀx*; if âᵢᵀx* > bᵢ + ε add âᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ. 4. No cut added ⇒ x* optimal; else go to 2.
cards.x: Re-solve with dual simplex: adding a constraint keeps the previous basis dual feasible, so it warm-starts.

cards.b: Start with U⁰ = {h^hist}. Solve master for z^κ; find h^κ = argmax_{h∈U} npr^κ(h, z^κ) (worst insufficiency); U^κ ← {h^hist, h¹, …, h^κ}; stop when the relative change in npr falls below η.
cards.x: Uncertainty is demand h; the robust constraint is npr ≥ Σ λ_w(h_{jsw} − Σ σ z) ∀h ∈ U.

cards.b: Cutting planes: any set whose inner max is solvable, no strong duality needed. Reformulation: one tractable counterpart. Both competitive; cutting planes tend to win on polyhedral sets, reformulation on ellipsoidal sets.
cards.x: Bertsimas, Dunning, Lubin (2016), Reformulation versus cutting-planes for robust optimization.

quiz.q: Why can't the robust LP with constraints aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ be passed directly to an LP solver?
o: It has infinitely many constraints when Uᵢ is infinite
Its objective cᵀx is nonlinear in x
quiz.e: One linear constraint per aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ. The feasible set is an intersection of half-spaces, hence convex; the obstacle is the number of constraints, not convexity.

quiz.q: A norm uncertainty set defined with the ℓ2 norm is called:
quiz.e: ℓ2 ↔ ellipsoidal, ℓ∞ ↔ box, ℓ1 ↔ budget.

quiz.q: The dual norm of the ℓ∞ norm is:
quiz.e: q = p/(p−1) → 1 as p → ∞. So a box set ‖uᵢ‖∞ ≤ ρ gives the buffer ρ‖Δᵢx‖₁.

quiz.q: The robust counterpart of an LP with ellipsoidal uncertainty sets is a:
quiz.e: The constraint āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≤ bᵢ is a second-order cone constraint. Box, budget and polyhedral sets keep it linear.

quiz.q: The robust counterpart of an LP with polyhedral uncertainty sets is a:
quiz.e: LP duality introduces pᵢ ≥ 0 with linear constraints pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ and āᵢᵀx + pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ, so everything stays linear.

quiz.q: In the cutting-plane algorithm, the master problem is initialized as:
o: The full robust problem, Ûᵢ = Uᵢ
quiz.e: Start with the nominal rows and add worst-case rows as cuts. Starting from Uᵢ would be the original intractable problem.

quiz.q: Dual norm of the ℓ3 norm?
quiz.e: q = p/(p−1) = 3/2 (equivalently 1/p + 1/q = 1). 2/3 inverts the formula and is not even a norm.

quiz.q: āᵢ = (2, 3), x = (1, 2), Δᵢ = I, ellipsoidal set with ρ = 0.5. Worst-case value of aᵢᵀx?
quiz.e: āᵢᵀx = 8; buffer ρ‖x‖₂ = 0.5√5 ≈ 1.12. 9.50 uses ‖x‖₁ = 3 (box set); 9.00 uses ‖x‖∞ = 2 (budget set).

quiz.q: Budget set ‖uᵢ‖₁ ≤ Γ with Γ = 2, Δᵢ = I, āᵢᵀx = 10, x = (3, −1, 2). Robust left-hand side?
quiz.e: Dual of ℓ1 is ℓ∞: 10 + 2·max(3, 1, 2) = 16. 22 uses ‖x‖₁ = 6 (box); ≈ 17.5 uses ‖x‖₂ = √14.

quiz.q: LP dual of the inner problem max uᵢᵀx s.t. Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ (uᵢ free):
o: min pᵢᵀdᵢ s.t. pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≥ 0
min pᵢᵀdᵢ s.t. pᵢᵀDᵢ ≥ xᵀ, pᵢ free
min pᵢᵀx s.t. Dᵢpᵢ = dᵢ, pᵢ ≥ 0
min pᵢᵀdᵢ s.t. pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≤ 0
quiz.e: Free primal variables ⇒ dual equality constraints; ≤ rows in a max ⇒ nonnegative multipliers. Inequality pᵢᵀDᵢ ≥ xᵀ would require uᵢ ≥ 0.

quiz.q: Polyhedral robust counterpart with n = 10 variables, m = 5 uncertain rows, ℓᵢ = 4 for every row. Variables and regular constraints?
quiz.e: Variables n + Σℓᵢ = 10 + 20 = 30. Constraints m + nm = 5 + 50 = 55: each pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ is n equalities. 10/5 is the ellipsoidal (same-size) case.

quiz.q: In the CLT-based set, what does −Γ√n ≤ Σⱼ uᵢⱼ ≤ Γ√n restrict?
o: The total of the scaled deviations across a row
The Euclidean norm of the deviation vector
The number of coefficients that may deviate
quiz.e: It is a global perturbation: individual uᵢⱼ may be large if they cancel. The element-wise box −Γ ≤ uᵢⱼ ≤ Γ restricts each separately.

quiz.q: The cutting-plane master problem is infeasible. What can you conclude?
o: Too many cuts were added; remove the latest
The tolerance ε is too small
The nominal problem is feasible but unbounded
quiz.e: Ûᵢ ⊆ Uᵢ, so the master is a relaxation: if it has no solution, neither does the robust problem. Cuts are valid robust constraints, so removing them is not justified.

quiz.q: At master solution x*, row i's subproblem returns âᵢ. When is the cut âᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ added?
quiz.e: Only violated worst cases produce cuts; if no row is violated beyond ε, x* is robust feasible and optimal.

quiz.q: Per the benchmark cited in lecture, which method tends to dominate with polyhedral uncertainty sets?
quiz.e: Bertsimas–Dunning–Lubin (2016): cutting planes tend to dominate with polyhedral sets, reformulation with ellipsoidal sets.

quiz.q: Same āᵢ, Δᵢ, x and ρ. Rank the robust buffers for box (‖u‖∞ ≤ ρ), ellipsoidal (‖u‖₂ ≤ ρ) and budget (‖u‖₁ ≤ ρ) sets.
o: All equal, since ρ is the same
quiz.e: Buffers are ρ‖Δᵢx‖₁ ≥ ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≥ ρ‖Δᵢx‖∞; equivalently the ℓ∞ ball contains the ℓ2 ball, which contains the ℓ1 ball. The reversed order confuses the set's norm with the buffer's.

quiz.q: Why does the duality method need the inner max rewritten as a min before adding pᵢ as variables?
o: min ≤ bᵢ holds iff some pᵢ satisfies it; max ≤ bᵢ must hold for every point
A min problem is always smaller than the max problem
The max problem is nonconvex in aᵢ
quiz.e: Existential conditions can be enforced by letting the solver choose a witness pᵢ; universal ones cannot. The inner max is an LP, so it is not nonconvex.

quiz.q: For the robust max cᵀx, how does the master objective behave across cutting-plane iterations?
o: An upper bound on the robust optimum, non-increasing as cuts are added
A lower bound on the robust optimum, non-decreasing
Equal to the robust optimum from the first iteration
Unrelated to the robust optimum until termination
quiz.e: The master is a relaxation of a maximization, so its value is ≥ the robust optimum; adding constraints can only lower it. Lower bounds would come from robust-feasible points.

quiz.q: In the robust nurse-scheduling cutting plane, the subproblem at iteration κ:
o: Finds demand h ∈ U maximizing insufficiency for the fixed schedule z^κ
Finds schedule z minimizing insufficiency for historical demand
Finds demand h ∈ U minimizing the number of nurse-shifts
Re-solves the master with all scenarios in U
quiz.e: Like âᵢ = argmax aᵢᵀx*, it finds the worst-case demand for the current schedule and adds it to U^κ. Optimizing z is the master's job.

quiz.q: For which situation does only the cutting-plane method apply, not reformulation?
o: The inner max is solvable but no strong-duality reformulation is available
The uncertainty set is an ellipsoid
The uncertainty set is a polyhedron with few facets
The nominal problem is an LP
quiz.e: Cutting planes need only an oracle for max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx and can be applied without strong duality. Ellipsoids and polyhedra have tractable counterparts, so both methods apply.

written.q: Consider max cᵀx s.t. aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Uᵢ, x ≥ 0, with Uᵢ = {āᵢ + Δᵢᵀuᵢ : ‖uᵢ‖₂ ≤ ρ}. Derive the robust counterpart, prove the inner maximization result, and state its problem class and size. How does the result change for a general norm?
written.m: Rewrite each row as max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ. Substituting aᵢ = āᵢ + Δᵢᵀuᵢ: max aᵢᵀx = āᵢᵀx + max_{‖uᵢ‖₂≤ρ} uᵢᵀ(Δᵢx). Take uᵢ* = ρΔᵢx/‖Δᵢx‖₂: feasible since ‖uᵢ*‖₂ = ρ, value ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂. Optimal by Cauchy–Schwarz: uᵢᵀ(Δᵢx) ≤ ‖uᵢ‖₂‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≤ ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂. Robust counterpart: max cᵀx s.t. āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ ≤ bᵢ ∀i, x ≥ 0, a second-order cone problem with n variables and m constraints, as many as the nominal LP; ρ‖Δᵢx‖₂ is a safety buffer growing with uncertainty. For a general norm, scale uᵢ = ρvᵢ with ‖vᵢ‖ ≤ 1 to get āᵢᵀx + ρ‖Δᵢx‖_* ≤ bᵢ, with ‖s‖_* = max_{‖x‖≤1}|sᵀx|: box (ℓ∞) → ℓ1 buffer, budget (ℓ1) → ℓ∞ buffer (both linear), ℓp → ℓq with q = p/(p−1).
k: Gives maximizer uᵢ* and checks feasibility
States SOCP and same size n, m
Generalizes to dual norm with correct pairs

written.q: Let Uᵢ = {āᵢ + uᵢ : Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ} with Dᵢ ∈ ℝ^{ℓᵢ×n}. Use LP duality to derive a tractable robust counterpart, explain why the dual variables can become decision variables, and give the counterpart's size.
written.m: Inner problem: max_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx = āᵢᵀx + max{uᵢᵀx : Dᵢuᵢ ≤ dᵢ}. Its LP dual is min{pᵢᵀdᵢ : pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≥ 0} (free uᵢ ⇒ equality; ≤ rows ⇒ pᵢ ≥ 0); by strong duality the values match when the inner problem is feasible and bounded. The robust row becomes āᵢᵀx + min_{pᵢ} pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ, and a min is ≤ bᵢ iff some feasible pᵢ achieves it, so: ∃pᵢ ≥ 0 with pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ and āᵢᵀx + pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ. Robust counterpart: max cᵀx s.t. pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, āᵢᵀx + pᵢᵀdᵢ ≤ bᵢ, pᵢ ≥ 0 ∀i, x ≥ 0, a linear program. Size: n + Σℓᵢ variables, m + nm regular constraints, n + Σℓᵢ nonnegativity constraints; it grows with the set description but is generally tractable.
k: Correct dual with pᵢᵀDᵢ = xᵀ, pᵢ ≥ 0

written.q: Describe the cutting-plane algorithm for a robust LP. Justify its infeasibility and optimality stopping rules, and explain when you would prefer it over a reformulation.
written.m: Maintain finite Ûᵢ ⊆ Uᵢ, initially {āᵢ} (the nominal problem). Master: max cᵀx s.t. aᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ ∀aᵢ ∈ Ûᵢ, x ≥ 0. If infeasible, stop: the master is a relaxation (fewer constraints than the robust problem), so the robust problem is infeasible. If unbounded, take an x* with a very large objective. Otherwise for each row solve âᵢ = argmax_{aᵢ∈Uᵢ} aᵢᵀx*; if âᵢᵀx* > bᵢ + ε, add âᵢᵀx ≤ bᵢ. Re-solve with dual simplex (warm start). If no cut is added, x* satisfies every robust row (up to ε) and is optimal for a relaxation, hence optimal for the robust problem. Prefer cutting planes when the inner max is easy but no strong-duality counterpart is available, and with polyhedral sets, where benchmarks (Bertsimas–Dunning–Lubin 2016) show it tends to dominate; reformulation tends to dominate with ellipsoidal sets. Example: robust nurse scheduling adds the demand scenario h maximizing insufficiency for the current schedule, stopping when npr's relative change falls below η.
k: Master over restricted sets, nominal start
When to prefer: no duality needed, polyhedral sets
